evaluations.bottleneck: Before Common Crawl, web-scale training text was impossible or impractical for most labs because assembling and licensing a petabyte-scale web corpus required proprietary crawling infrastructure.

Q11.evidence: Filtered Common Crawl was the largest single component of GPT-3's training mix by token count.
Q11.falsification: This pass dies if the actual GPT-3 training mix was dominated by other corpora.

Q12.evidence: Open web-scale corpora derived from Common Crawl, such as C4 and RefinedWeb, became the default starting point for LLM pretraining.
Q12.falsification: This pass dies if the field reverted to purely proprietary, closed corpora as the norm.

Q2.evidence: GPT-3 was trained largely on a filtered Common Crawl corpus, and the same free corpus seeded many later open language models.
Q2.falsification: This pass dies if GPT-class models are shown to have relied negligibly on Common Crawl data.

Q4.evidence: Common Crawl distributes petabytes of crawled web data free of charge, removing the crawl cost entirely for downstream labs.
Q4.falsification: This pass dies if comparable web-scale corpora were already freely available at similar scale before 2007.

Q7.evidence: Common Crawl publishes data in standard WARC/WAT formats that any lab can consume without building its own crawler.
Q7.falsification: This pass dies if consumers in practice had to build bespoke ingestion for each release.

evaluations.bottleneck: Before Linux, running large server and cluster fleets was impractical at low cost because Unix systems were proprietary and per-machine licensed.

Q10.evidence: Linux displaced proprietary Unix as the default server and supercomputer operating system, reaching 100% of the TOP500 by 2017.
Q10.falsification: This pass dies if proprietary Unix retained the majority of supercomputing installations.

Q11.evidence: Major ML frameworks and GPU training stacks are developed and deployed Linux-first.
Q11.falsification: This pass dies if the main LLM training stacks were developed primarily for another OS.

Q12.evidence: Cloud and HPC infrastructure standardized on Linux and container images built on it, with no movement back to proprietary Unix.
Q12.falsification: This pass dies if a proprietary OS reclaimed the server and HPC default.

Q2.evidence: Linux came to run essentially all TOP500 supercomputers and the large majority of cloud servers on which model training clusters are built.
Q2.falsification: This pass dies if AI training infrastructure in fact ran mainly on non-Linux systems.

Q4.evidence: Linux is free and open source, eliminating per-server operating-system licensing costs across entire data centers.
Q4.falsification: This pass dies if total OS cost was never a material constraint on cluster scale.

Q7.evidence: Linux exposes the POSIX interface, so training frameworks, containers and schedulers build on it without regard to hardware internals.
Q7.falsification: This pass dies if ML tooling in practice targeted hardware directly rather than the OS abstraction.

Q8.evidence: Linux dominates servers, supercomputing, embedded systems and Android devices simultaneously.
Q8.falsification: This pass dies if Linux remained confined to a single niche.

evaluations.bottleneck: Before Python, ML experimentation was impractical at speed because research code had to be written in low-level or statistically niche languages with slow edit-test cycles.

Q10.evidence: Python displaced R, MATLAB and Lua/Torch as the default language of ML research during the deep learning era.
Q10.falsification: This pass dies if another language held the majority of new ML framework adoption.

Q11.evidence: The canonical agent frameworks and LLM APIs of 2023 onward shipped Python SDKs first.
Q11.falsification: This pass dies if agent tooling of that period was primarily non-Python.

Q2.evidence: PyTorch, TensorFlow, Hugging Face and LangChain-style agent scaffolding are all Python-first, making one language serve the whole agent stack.
Q2.falsification: This pass dies if the main agent frameworks were in fact built primarily in other languages.

Q4.evidence: Python's interpreted, high-level syntax plus NumPy vectorization cut the code and time needed for numerical experiments by large factors versus C implementations.
Q4.falsification: This pass dies if measured researcher productivity in Python matched that in lower-level languages.

Q7.evidence: Python became the standard interface layer: frameworks expose Python APIs over C++/CUDA internals that users never inspect.
Q7.falsification: This pass dies if practitioners routinely had to work below the Python API to use these frameworks.

Q8.evidence: Python is a top language across data science, web backends, automation and scientific computing, not only ML.
Q8.falsification: This pass dies if Python use remained confined to machine learning.

Q9.evidence: Interactive notebooks and interpreted execution let researchers test a model change in seconds rather than a compile-run cycle.
Q9.falsification: This pass dies if ML iteration in practice remained dominated by compiled-language workflows.

evaluations.bottleneck: Before arXiv, ML results were impractical to obtain quickly because dissemination waited on journal and conference publication cycles of months to years.

Q12.evidence: Preprint-first dissemination became the entrenched norm in ML, with major results expected on arXiv at announcement.
Q12.falsification: This pass dies if ML venues returned to journal-first release as the norm.

Q4.evidence: arXiv posting is free and makes a paper globally available within days, versus months of review and paywalled distribution.
Q4.falsification: This pass dies if preprint posting carried comparable cost and delay to journal publication.

Q8.evidence: arXiv serves physics, mathematics, computer science, biology, finance and statistics from one preprint infrastructure.
Q8.falsification: This pass dies if arXiv remained a single-field archive.

Q9.evidence: Agent techniques such as the ReAct paper circulated and were reimplemented within weeks of arXiv posting, before any formal publication.
Q9.falsification: This pass dies if uptake of such papers in practice waited for peer-reviewed publication.

evaluations.bottleneck: Before Wikipedia, a large clean encyclopedic text corpus was impractical to assemble because reference content was proprietary, paywalled or too small.

Q4.evidence: Wikipedia provides millions of articles under a free license at zero acquisition cost, replacing licensed encyclopedia corpora.
Q4.falsification: This pass dies if an equally large free encyclopedic corpus already existed before 2001.

evaluations.bottleneck: Before Linnainmaa's automatic differentiation, exact gradients of nested functions were impractical because numerical differentiation was inaccurate and symbolic differentiation blew up in expression size.

Q1.evidence: Linnainmaa's 1970 thesis gave reverse-mode differentiation, computing exact derivatives of a nested function in a single backward pass proportional to function evaluation cost.
Q1.falsification: This pass dies if an equally efficient exact gradient method for nested functions predates 1970.
Q1.source: The representation of the cumulative rounding error of an algorithm as a Taylor expansion of the local rounding errors

Q10.evidence: Autodiff displaced hand-coded gradient derivations as the default in every major deep learning framework.
Q10.falsification: This pass dies if hand-derived gradients remained the framework default.
Q10.source: The representation of the cumulative rounding error of an algorithm as a Taylor expansion of the local rounding errors

Q11.evidence: Backpropagation as implemented in all LLM training is reverse-mode autodiff applied to a neural network graph.
Q11.falsification: This pass dies if LLM training gradients are computed by a lineage independent of reverse-mode autodiff.
Q11.source: The representation of the cumulative rounding error of an algorithm as a Taylor expansion of the local rounding errors

Q12.evidence: No subsequent training paradigm has displaced reverse-mode autodiff; even alternative methods are benchmarked against it.
Q12.falsification: This pass dies if a non-autodiff method becomes the default for training large models.
Q12.source: The representation of the cumulative rounding error of an algorithm as a Taylor expansion of the local rounding errors

Q2.evidence: Reverse-mode autodiff underlies training of every modern neural network, from MLPs to billion-parameter transformers.
Q2.falsification: This pass dies if large networks were in practice trained by a method independent of reverse-mode gradients.
Q2.source: The representation of the cumulative rounding error of an algorithm as a Taylor expansion of the local rounding errors

Q3.evidence: For models with millions of parameters and one scalar loss, reverse mode is asymptotically the only tractable exact gradient method; finite differences would need one evaluation per parameter.
Q3.falsification: This pass dies if a comparably cheap alternative gradient method exists for scalar-loss, many-parameter models.
Q3.source: The representation of the cumulative rounding error of an algorithm as a Taylor expansion of the local rounding errors

Q4.evidence: Reverse mode computes all parameter gradients at a cost within a small constant factor of one forward evaluation, versus one evaluation per parameter for finite differences.
Q4.falsification: This pass dies if its gradient cost in fact scaled linearly with parameter count.
Q4.source: The representation of the cumulative rounding error of an algorithm as a Taylor expansion of the local rounding errors

Q6.evidence: The thesis modeled a computation as a composition of elementary operations whose derivatives chain, the computational-graph model every autodiff framework implements.
Q6.falsification: This pass dies if modern frameworks do not in fact represent programs as differentiable operation graphs.
Q6.source: The representation of the cumulative rounding error of an algorithm as a Taylor expansion of the local rounding errors

Q7.evidence: PyTorch and TensorFlow expose autodiff as an abstraction: users write forward code and call backward without deriving gradients by hand.
Q7.falsification: This pass dies if framework users still had to hand-derive gradients for new operations as the norm.
Q7.source: The representation of the cumulative rounding error of an algorithm as a Taylor expansion of the local rounding errors

Q8.evidence: Automatic differentiation is used across physics simulation, optimization, robotics and computational science, well beyond neural networks.
Q8.falsification: This pass dies if autodiff use remained confined to neural network training.
Q8.source: The representation of the cumulative rounding error of an algorithm as a Taylor expansion of the local rounding errors

evaluations.bottleneck: Before energy-based models, associative memory and probabilistic neural computation were impractical because there was no principled framework for network states to settle into stored patterns.

Q6.evidence: Hopfield's 1982 energy function showed a network's dynamics minimize a Lyapunov energy, giving a designable model of content-addressable memory.
Q6.falsification: This pass dies if the energy formulation did not in fact predict or guide network behavior.

evaluations.bottleneck: Before simulated annealing, escaping local optima in combinatorial problems was impractical because greedy methods had no principled mechanism for accepting worsening moves.

Q8.evidence: Simulated annealing was applied to VLSI placement, scheduling and many other combinatorial problems far outside its metallurgical origin.
Q8.falsification: This pass dies if its documented applications stayed within one field.

evaluations.bottleneck: Before Bayesian networks, reasoning under uncertainty over many variables was impractical because full joint probability tables grow exponentially in the number of variables.

Q2.evidence: Factoring a joint distribution into a directed graph of conditional dependencies made probabilistic models tractable across diagnosis, genetics and decision analysis.
Q2.falsification: This pass dies if graphical factorization did not in fact enable models that were previously intractable.
Q2.source: Fusion, propagation, and structuring in belief networks - ACM Digital Library

Q6.evidence: Pearl's framework explained inference as message passing over a dependency graph, enabling deliberate design of probabilistic reasoning systems.
Q6.falsification: This pass dies if practitioners did not use the graph semantics to design inference systems.
Q6.source: Fusion, propagation, and structuring in belief networks - ACM Digital Library

Q7.evidence: Probabilistic graphical models became a standard abstraction implemented in reusable inference libraries and textbooks.
Q7.falsification: This pass dies if the formalism was never packaged as a reusable modeling standard.
Q7.source: Fusion, propagation, and structuring in belief networks - ACM Digital Library

Q8.evidence: Bayesian networks were adopted in medicine, genetics, fault diagnosis and risk analysis beyond their AI origin.
Q8.falsification: This pass dies if adoption stayed inside AI research.
Q8.source: Fusion, propagation, and structuring in belief networks - ACM Digital Library

evaluations.bottleneck: Before dynamic programming, optimal sequential decision-making was impossible to compute systematically because the space of action sequences grows exponentially with horizon length.

Q1.evidence: Bellman's principle of optimality reduced sequential decision problems to recursive value equations solvable stage by stage instead of by enumerating all action sequences.
Q1.falsification: This pass dies if an equally general tractable method for sequential decisions predates Bellman.

Q11.evidence: Temporal-difference learning, Q-learning and policy-gradient methods in the direct ancestry of RLHF are all Bellman-equation methods.
Q11.falsification: This pass dies if those methods' derivations do not use Bellman recursions.

Q12.evidence: The MDP/Bellman framework remains the unchallenged baseline formalism for sequential decision-making after nearly seventy years.
Q12.falsification: This pass dies if a successor formalism displaces Bellman recursion as the RL default.

Q2.evidence: The Bellman equation underlies reinforcement learning, operations research, economics and control, a whole space of sequential-decision methods.
Q2.falsification: This pass dies if value-function recursion remained confined to one problem type.

Q3.evidence: RLHF and RL-trained agents optimize value and policy functions defined by Bellman recursions; no alternative formalism supplies that machinery in the actual lineage.
Q3.falsification: This pass dies if the RL used for modern agents is shown to rest on a non-Bellman foundation.

Q6.evidence: The value function gave a deliberate design model: specify rewards, compute or approximate values, and derive optimal actions.
Q6.falsification: This pass dies if RL system design did not in fact proceed via value and reward specification.

Q7.evidence: States, actions, rewards and value functions became the standard MDP interface on which RL algorithms and agent environments are built.
Q7.falsification: This pass dies if RL environments do not in practice expose this interface.

Q8.evidence: Dynamic programming reshaped economics, operations research, bioinformatics sequence alignment and control engineering.
Q8.falsification: This pass dies if its influence stayed within control theory.

evaluations.bottleneck: Before AlphaGo, superhuman play in Go was impractical because the game's branching factor defeated hand-crafted evaluation and pure search.
Before dropout, training very large networks was impractical because co-adapted units overfit training data and destroyed generalization.
Before the attention mechanism, neural sequence models were impractical on long inputs because a single fixed-length vector had to carry the entire source sequence.

Q1.evidence: Bahdanau attention let the decoder align to relevant source words at each step, restoring translation quality on long sentences that fixed-vector seq2seq models lost.
Q1.falsification: This pass dies if fixed-vector models matched attention models on long sentences in the original comparisons.
Q1.source: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate - arXiv

Q10.evidence: Attention-based Transformers displaced recurrent seq2seq models as the default sequence architecture within a few years.
Q10.falsification: This pass dies if recurrent architectures retained the majority of sequence-model deployments.
Q10.source: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate - arXiv

Q11.evidence: The historical line Bahdanau attention to Transformer to GPT-class models to LLM agents is direct and documented.
Q11.falsification: This pass dies if GPT-class models are shown to descend from a separate, attention-free lineage.
Q11.source: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate - arXiv

Q12.evidence: Attention remains the core operation of frontier models a decade later, with alternatives still measured against it.
Q12.falsification: This pass dies if attention-free architectures become the frontier default.
Q12.source: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate - arXiv

Q2.evidence: Generalizing attention to self-attention produced the Transformer, which unblocked modern LLMs and hence LLM agents.
Q2.falsification: This pass dies if the Transformer's self-attention is shown to derive independently of Bahdanau-style alignment.
Q2.source: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate - arXiv

Q3.evidence: Every production LLM agent runs on a Transformer whose core operation descends directly from learned soft alignment introduced here.
Q3.falsification: This pass dies if a non-attention architecture, not the Transformer, powered the 2023 agent wave.
Q3.source: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate - arXiv

Q6.evidence: Attention supplied an explicit model of relevance weighting over context, letting designers reason about and engineer context use deliberately.
Q6.falsification: This pass dies if attention weights played no role in subsequent architecture design decisions.
Q6.source: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate - arXiv

Q7.evidence: Attention became a standard composable layer (multi-head, cross-attention) reused across translation, vision and multimodal models.
Q7.falsification: This pass dies if attention remained a one-off trick inside a single translation system.
Q7.source: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate - arXiv

Q8.evidence: Attention-based architectures spread to vision (ViT), speech, protein modeling and multimodal systems far beyond translation.
Q8.falsification: This pass dies if attention stayed confined to machine translation.
Q8.source: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate - arXiv

evaluations.bottleneck: Before the ReAct agent pattern, LLM tool use was impractical because reasoning and acting were separate: models either answered in one shot or acted without revisable, feedback-driven plans.

Q1.evidence: ReAct showed an LLM interleaving reasoning traces with actions and observations could solve multi-step tasks like HotpotQA and ALFWorld that chain-of-thought or action-only baselines handled worse.
Q1.falsification: This pass dies if the paper's own baselines matched ReAct on those interactive benchmarks.
Q1.source: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models - arXiv

Q11.evidence: ReAct is the named architectural ancestor cited by the 2023 wave of LLM agent frameworks.
Q11.falsification: This pass dies if 2023 agent frameworks are shown to derive from an unrelated loop design without citing ReAct.
Q11.source: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models - arXiv

Q2.evidence: The reason-act-observe loop generalized across question answering, web shopping, household simulation and later tool-using and coding agents.
Q2.falsification: This pass dies if the pattern proved usable for only one benchmark task.
Q2.source: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models - arXiv

Q6.evidence: ReAct gave a deliberate design model for agents: emit a thought, take an action, read the observation, and revise, which framework builders adopted as a template.
Q6.falsification: This pass dies if agent frameworks did not adopt the thought-action-observation template.
Q6.source: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models - arXiv

Q7.evidence: LangChain and similar frameworks implemented ReAct as a named, reusable agent type that developers invoke without designing the loop themselves.
Q7.falsification: This pass dies if no major framework shipped ReAct as a standard agent abstraction.
Q7.source: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models - arXiv

Q8.evidence: The pattern was applied in research agents, customer-support automation, software engineering agents and robotics task planning.
Q8.falsification: This pass dies if ReAct use stayed within academic QA benchmarks.
Q8.source: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models - arXiv

evaluations.bottleneck: Before ELIZA, conversational interaction with a computer was impractical for non-specialists because interfaces required formal command languages.
Before Shakey the Robot, integrated perception, planning and action in one machine was impossible because sensing, world modeling and planning existed only as separate programs.
Before Lisp, symbolic computation was impractical because existing languages were built for numeric processing and lacked recursion, dynamic lists and garbage collection.
Before Logic Theorist, automated reasoning was impossible to demonstrate because no program had performed heuristic search to prove a formal theorem.
Before the Dartmouth Workshop, machine intelligence research was impractical to organize because it had no name, shared agenda or convened research community.
Before expert systems, deploying specialist knowledge in software was impractical because expertise lived only in human experts and could not be encoded for machine inference.
Before Prolog, mechanized logical inference was impractical because programmers had to specify search procedures explicitly instead of stating facts and rules declaratively.
Before the Turing Test proposal, evaluating machine intelligence was impractical because there was no operational criterion, only philosophical argument about thinking.

Q5.evidence: The imitation game turned intelligence into an observable behavioral measurement: a judge's ability to distinguish machine from human in conversation.
Q5.falsification: This pass dies if the paper proposed no judge-based behavioral measurement.

Q6.evidence: Turing's operational reframing, plus his anticipation of learning machines, gave researchers a design target of indistinguishability rather than a definition of thought.
Q6.falsification: This pass dies if the paper offered only a philosophical definition with no operational target.

evaluations.bottleneck: Before the McCulloch-Pitts neuron, neural computation was impossible to formalize because there was no mathematical model of a neuron as a computing unit.

Q1.evidence: The 1943 paper showed threshold-logic neurons could compute logical functions, making neural networks a formal object of computation for the first time.
Q1.falsification: This pass dies if an earlier formal neuron model with equivalent computational results exists.
Q1.source: A logical calculus of the ideas immanent in nervous activity - Bulletin of Mathematical Biophysics

Q11.evidence: The perceptron and every subsequent neural architecture explicitly build on the McCulloch-Pitts unit, placing it at the root of the lineage to LLMs.
Q11.falsification: This pass dies if the perceptron lineage is shown to originate elsewhere.
Q11.source: A logical calculus of the ideas immanent in nervous activity - Bulletin of Mathematical Biophysics

Q12.evidence: The neuron-as-unit abstraction has never been abandoned; even Transformers are stacks of neuron layers.
Q12.falsification: This pass dies if frontier models cease to be built from neuron units.
Q12.source: A logical calculus of the ideas immanent in nervous activity - Bulletin of Mathematical Biophysics

Q2.evidence: Networks of these units founded the entire neural network research program from perceptrons to deep learning.
Q2.falsification: This pass dies if later neural network research is shown to descend from an independent formalism.
Q2.source: A logical calculus of the ideas immanent in nervous activity - Bulletin of Mathematical Biophysics

Q6.evidence: Modeling neurons as threshold logic units explained nervous activity in logical terms and let researchers design networks by composition of units.
Q6.falsification: This pass dies if the model had no influence on how later networks were designed.
Q6.source: A logical calculus of the ideas immanent in nervous activity - Bulletin of Mathematical Biophysics

Q7.evidence: The artificial neuron became the standard composable unit from which perceptrons, MLPs and deep networks are all assembled.
Q7.falsification: This pass dies if modern networks are not in fact assembled from neuron-like units.
Q7.source: A logical calculus of the ideas immanent in nervous activity - Bulletin of Mathematical Biophysics

Q8.evidence: The model influenced neuroscience theory, logic and automata theory as well as computer science.
Q8.falsification: This pass dies if its documented influence stayed inside one discipline.
Q8.source: A logical calculus of the ideas immanent in nervous activity - Bulletin of Mathematical Biophysics

evaluations.bottleneck: Before the General Problem Solver, general-purpose machine problem solving was impractical because each program solved one fixed task with no reusable goal-directed method.

Q6.evidence: Means-ends analysis modeled problem solving as repeatedly reducing the difference between current and goal states, a schema later planners deliberately implemented.
Q6.falsification: This pass dies if later planning systems did not adopt difference-reduction as a design schema.
Q6.source: Report on a general problem-solving program - ACM Digital Library

evaluations.bottleneck: Before Deep Blue, defeating a world chess champion by computer was impractical because search speed and position evaluation were insufficient at tournament scale.
Before TD-Gammon, learning expert game play from self-play alone was impractical because supervised training required large corpora of expert-labeled positions.

Q2.evidence: TD-Gammon's self-play temporal-difference learning demonstrated a general route later scaled by AlphaGo-style systems and RL training pipelines.
Q2.falsification: This pass dies if later self-play RL systems are shown to owe nothing to the TD self-play demonstration.
Q2.source: Practical Issues in Temporal Difference Learning - Springer

Q6.evidence: TD-Gammon validated the model that value estimates can be bootstrapped from successive self-generated predictions, guiding deliberate RL system design.
Q6.falsification: This pass dies if bootstrapped value learning was not taken up as a design principle after TD-Gammon.
Q6.source: Practical Issues in Temporal Difference Learning - Springer

evaluations.bottleneck: Before Dragon NaturallySpeaking, continuous speech dictation on a personal computer was impractical because recognizers required pausing between words and extensive per-speaker training.
Before Siri, a voice assistant on a mass consumer device was impractical because natural-language request handling and service delegation had not been packaged into a phone.

Before Watson (Jeopardy!), open-domain question answering over unstructured text was impractical at champion level because retrieval and answer confidence scoring could not be combined at the required speed and accuracy.
